# read_C: pp. 60–62 (leaves n61–n63), established from the images

Line counts: p. 60 has five lines (a leaf back, no ornament; checked). p. 61 has five lines (a leaf front, opens ༄༅༔ ༔, both ༔ clear). p. 62 has five lines (a leaf back, no ornament). That makes 15 print lines.
The witness's line breaks match the print on every line (15 of 15).

**End of the part.** 62.5 ends …དེ་ལྟར་ཡིན་པར་ངོ་ཤེས་པར་གྱིས་ཤིག༔, with the ༔ standing just before the right frame (×3, n63). A sentence closes there ("…recognise that it is so"). The next sentence, about the size of the deities (the other recension has ཀྱེ་རིགས་ཀྱི་བུ་སྐུ་དེ་དག་མི་ཆེ་བ…), starts on p. 63. So the part ends at the end of p. 62 l. 5, as planned. n64 was not needed.

Method: line bands were located from the row profile (headlines n61 at y≈110/170/225/280/335, n62 ≈95/155/210/265/320, n63 ≈160/215/270/320/375). Each line was cropped in four overlapping segments at ×3 (LANCZOS), and doubtful syllables at ×5–×10, with a pixel dump (threshold 128) where the shapes were too small to judge by eye.
The tsheg before ༔ was checked for every ༔ on the three pages. A template match on the ༔ shape (threshold 0.38) found them all. One missed instance, 61.2 བུ༔, was dumped by hand. For each ༔, the gap between the preceding letter and the ༔ was then inspected as a pixel dump. A tsheg was counted when a separate blob of 4–6 px stood at headline height in that gap, or when such a blob hung below the end of the head bar.

- 60.5 (line end) ཞིང་: the tsheg is fused to the end of the head bar (see the table). If the drafter reads no tsheg here, the join 60.5 → 61.1 crosses the leaf-front ornament: ཞིང | ༄༅༔ ༔ཁམས་ནས. That needs a `# fix` of the form `# fix: ཞིང༄༅༔ ༔ཁམས => ཞིང་༄༅༔ ༔ཁམས`, depending on how the build joins across an ornament. With the tsheg as read, nothing is needed.

- The fused tshegs before ༔ on p. 61 (listed above): kept, as in the witness.

## Fixes needed (`# fix:` lines)

```
# fix: ཅན་གྱིཞིང་ཁམས => ཅན་གྱི་ཞིང་ཁམས
# fix: ད་ལྟ་འཆརརོ༔ => ད་ལྟ་འཆར་རོ༔
# fix: ༔ ལྷའིཐུབ་པ => ༔ ལྷའི་ཐུབ་པ
# fix: ཞིག་ནསའོང་བ => ཞིག་ནས་འོང་བ
```
These are the joins 60.4→60.5, 61.1→61.2, 61.3→61.4 and 62.4→62.5. In each, the last letter of the line meets the frame or clear space with no tsheg. None of these joins crosses a page-opening ornament. The only join that does is 60.5→61.1, and it has a tsheg as read (see the close call above).

No line-end abbreviations or contractions (པའཾ, ལཾ, ནམཁའ, subscript-ས) occur on these pages.

## Suspected misprints

1. 61.2 **གཞིན་རྗེ་གཤེད་པོ**, which should be གཤིན་རྗེ (Yamāntaka, "Slayer of the Lord of Death"; the other recension has གཤིན་རྗེའི་གཤེད་པོ). ཞ for ཤ: the image shows ཞ, and the witness typed ཞ too. The sense allows only one reading. Certainty is moderate to high (a one-stroke difference between ཞ and ཤ in this cut, but three shapes were compared). Proposed `# fix: གཞིན་རྗེ => གཤིན་རྗེ` as a misprint correction (rule 5b, print's reading in the note).
2. 60.5 རབ་རྫོགས against 53.4 རབ་བརྩེགས (part 005), for the same northern realm of Amoghasiddhi: an inconsistency inside the print, not a misprint in this line. རབ་རྫོགས is the usual name and the other recension's. Kept, note only. It may be worth noting at 53.4 that the print itself has རབ་རྫོགས here.

Not misprints, the print's own spelling: འཁྱིལ་པ, ཕྱི་རིམ, སྤྱི་མེས, ཀྱེ/ཀྱཻ beside each other, ཤཱཀྱ་སེངྒེ.

## Proposed name

For my stretch: `# name: Day six: all forty-two peaceful deities appear at once, from your own heart`.
The part as a whole (pp. 54–62) begins with Amoghasiddhi's retinue on day five. If readers A and B confirm that day five closes and day six opens inside the part, a name for the whole would be `# name: Day five, Amoghasiddhi; day six, the forty-two deities at once`.
